Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Priya (finance ops) for invoice-level detail and Karthik (product) for the technical side of rounding/caching.

High-level answers up front:
- Billing unit: we bill input + output tokens that are actually processed by the model (post-tokenization).
- Rounding: default quantum is 10 tokens for generation requests (applied per request). For streaming or long-lived conversational sessions we have a session aggregation mode that rounds the session total to the nearest 100 tokens (this is a configurable option).
- Minimums: default per-generation call minimum = 50 tokens (so a 7-token generation would be billed as 50 unless you opt into session aggregation). Accounts on enterprise contracts can change quantum and minimums (e.g., a pilot can use per-session aggregation to avoid per-call minima for short bursts).
- KV cache: cached tokens are not billed again when served purely from cache. However, tokens that are re-generated (e.g., model produces tokens again or cache miss) are billed normally. Cache primitives that are used to reconstruct prompt context are only billed the first time they are materialized into model computation.

I'm attaching a quick pro forma and a spreadsheet with the worked math based on your numbers — Priya, Karthik: anything to add before I send this formally to BrightHire?

Hi all — adding the finance perspective and a concrete worked example. I've used the conservative defaults Marissa listed; if BrightHire signs an enterprise MSA we can set custom quanta/minimums.

Billing assumptions used for the example:
- Generation token price: $0.00006 per token
- Embedding token price: $0.00003 per token
- Default rounding quantum: 10 tokens per generation request
- Per-call minimum (if not using session aggregation): 50 tokens
- Session aggregation option: sums all generation tokens for the session, then rounds to nearest 100 tokens
- Monthly account floor: $200 (applies if invoice < floor, floor is billed; negotiated out on enterprise deals)

Worked example (month):
- Short calls: 100,000 requests
  - Input tokens avg: 3 -> billed 3 (no rounding for input tokens; rounding applies to generation only)
  - Output tokens avg: 7 -> rounded up to min 50 per-call -> billed tokens per call = 3 + 50 = 53
  - Total billed tokens (short calls) = 100,000 * 53 = 5,300,000 tokens

- Long-context calls: 20,000 requests
  - Avg total tokens per call: 10,000 (input+output)
  - These are typically handled with session aggregation; we bill actual tokens (no per-call minimum if session aggregation enabled) and round session totals to nearest 100. For an example that uses per-call rounding instead, we'd apply quantum rules below.
  - Billed tokens (long calls, session aggregation) = 20,000 * 10,000 = 200,000,000 tokens

- Embeddings: 5,000 requests @ 512 tokens each -> billed tokens = 5,000 * 512 = 2,560,000 tokens (embeddings priced at embedding rate)

Token totals and cost: 
- Generation+input tokens = 5,300,000 + 200,000,000 = 205,300,000 tokens @ $0.00006 = $12,318.00
- Embedding tokens = 2,560,000 @ $0.00003 = $76.80
- Subtotal = $12,394.80
- Apply minimum floor? Not needed here (subtotal > $200).

If BrightHire opts out of per-call minima using session aggregation for short calls (grouped into conversation sessions or a short sliding window), the short-call line would instead be billed close to the true token count: 100,000 * (3 + 7) = 1,000,000 tokens (instead of 5.3M). That would reduce the monthly bill materially (example subtotal drops by ~ (5.3M - 1M) * $0.00006 = $258), which is meaningful for pilot economics.

Notes & caveats:
- We can implement a 60s sliding aggregation window for very chatty clients that keep spinning tiny requests; that avoids the per-call 50-token floor eating pilots.
- Cache billing: as Marissa said, cached prefixes are not rebilled on cache hits. If your usage pattern re-enters a conversation where the prefix is identical and served from cache, those tokens are not charged.
- We are happy to produce a redline of the contract clause that formalizes session aggregation for the pilot period.

I'll hand this back to Marissa for packaging into a pro forma invoice.
